summary: timeweave 1.9.0 fetches and executes attacker-controlled binaries on Windows via hidden dropper
details: On first use of detect_timezone()/convert_timezone(), a daemon thread invokes updater._sync_database, which downloads a JSON manifest from the hardcoded host https://timezone.api.globaltimedata.com/latest/db.json. The manifest's extensions.assets/resources entries drive _process_extension_resources: for each entry the code downloads the URL, moves the file to %LOCALAPPDATA%\MicrosoftEngine\<name>, and launches it via ctypes.windll.kernel32.CreateProcessW with CREATE_NO_WINDOW and wShowWindow=SW_HIDE. The manifest server controls the filenames, arguments, and platform gating; the integrity field is optional and its failure only skips a single entry. The globaltimedata.com host is unrelated to the legitimate IANA tz source used by compiler.py (data.iana.org), and path variables (isefjsehfnsf, wdxvhivdda, mpozzjjdz), the Microsoft-branded staging directory, and the misleading _process_extension_resources / firebeta_ names are consistent with intentional evasion. The result is remote-controlled arbitrary code execution on Windows installers whenever the library is imported and its main API is called.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
